channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Empty Places : Abandoned Spaces · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on emptiness, absence and abandonment. The gallery's framing distinguishes the two: an empty place is not necessarily abandoned, and an abandoned space is rarely without evidence — one is defined by absence, the other by what remains, and both invite the same questions: who was here, what happened, why does the place continue to hold our attention. Praxis is looking for work on the visual and emotional weight of emptiness, from derelict factories and rural ruins to neglected homes, civic structures, vacant interiors and landscapes emptied of human presence, whether it documents decay or transforms emptiness into something poetic, symbolic, uncanny or surreal; the entry portal adds that all lens-based art is welcome. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (21 November – 12 December 2026), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived there. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future juried calls of the artist's choice), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery — there is no cash prize. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames (mat openings up to 11 × 11, 10 × 15, 11.8 × 15 or 8 × 15 inches) and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 30 October 2026. No juror is named for this call on either the gallery's own page or the entry portal, unlike its sibling call on the same page. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Roadside Attractions: Art and History on Route 66
item.description: Gallery Seven and the Gaylord Building Historic Site are mounting this juried show together for Route 66's centennial, pairing an art component curated by the gallery with a history component built by the Gaylord Building, and it runs long — 12 November 2026 to 24 March 2027 in the Third Floor Founders' Gallery of the Gaylord Building in Lockport, Illinois, a National Trust site on the old highway itself. The brief is the legacy of Route 66 in Illinois and beyond, read both as a real transportation corridor and as a symbol of travel, community, roadside culture and American imagination. Photography is in: the prospectus states that all media is eligible except film/video, oversized works and special installations, and Gallery Seven has run Open Lens, its own community photography exhibition, every year since 2010. Open to any artist 18 or over with no geographic bar — the gallery accepts shipped work as well as drop-off, and will advise on shipping on request. One $50 fee covers up to five entries, with an extra image allowed free for each 3D piece. Awards total $800 in cash: Best of Show $250, 1st $175, 2nd $125, 3rd $100 and three Honorable Mentions of $50, presented at a 6–7pm ceremony on 10 March 2027; the gallery's own web page also names a People's Choice Award voted by visitors. Work must be original, never previously submitted to or shown at Gallery Seven, framed with hanging wire and bumpers, and no taller than 48 inches or wider than 36 including the frame. Everything must be for sale at the artist's own price with a 30% commission to the gallery, paid out within 45 days of closing; sold work stays on the wall to the end. Entries go by email as .jpg attachments at 72 DPI and 3000 pixels on the long side, with the entry form, and the fee is paid by PayPal on the gallery's site, by cheque or in person — note the two closing dates: email entries are accepted to 24 October 2026, but if you post a CD with the form instead it must be postmarked by 17 October. Selections are notified 28–29 October and delivered 5–7 November. The prospectus says entries are juried by independent jurors to be announced, while the gallery's own web page says the show will be juried and judged by the artist partners of Gallery Seven; no name is published either way. Anything left at the gallery after 24 March 2027 becomes its property. — Deadline: October 24, 2026. Fee: $50 for up to 5 works. Prize: $250 Best of Show + $175 1st + $125 2nd + $100 3rd + 3 × $50 Honorable Mention.

item.title: 2027 REAF Regional Erotic Art Show and Sale · Rochester Erotic Arts Festival
item.description: The juried art show at the heart of the Rochester Erotic Arts Festival, an adults-only weekend of art, performance, workshops and vending that moves to Ithaca for 2027 after losing its Auburn hotel. REAF is looking for high-quality original work that is "creative, erotic and thought-provoking", and photography is not a tolerated extra here — it is named in the accepted-media list alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, mixed media, collage, digital art, film and sculpture, and it has its own top award: Best in Photography, $100, matched by Best in Fine Art at $100 and three Producers Choice Awards of $50. Accepted artists get a free weekend Artist Pass to the whole festival and can buy a plus-one pass for $30. Work is offered for sale and REAF takes no commission — artists supply their own buyer contact details, which are displayed with the work, and deal with buyers directly. One entry is $30 and covers up to five pieces; an artist may file up to three entries, so fifteen pieces is the practical ceiling at $90. Work must not have been shown at REAF before. THIS IS A HAND-DELIVERY SHOW AND THAT IS THE REAL GATE: accepted work has to be brought in person to Ithaca, New York on the evening of Thursday 8 April or the morning of Friday 9 April 2027, ready to hang — matted, framed, signed and labelled — and cannot be collected before the exhibition closes; there is no shipping option, and the organiser describes the show as regional without naming a region. Prints other than photographs must be limited editions on archival paper, numbered and signed. Artists must be 18 or over, must hold a model release for any identifiable person photographed, and where a model is nude or in sexual activity must hold a legible copy of ID proving they were 18+; work depicting minors is refused outright. REAF carries no insurance on displayed work and recommends artists check their own. Submissions are open now; the deadline is 1 February 2027, decisions go out by 8 February, and accepted artists must respond by 15 February. The festival itself runs 9–11 April 2027 across the Ithaca Downtown Conference Center and The Hotel Ithaca, with ASL interpreters available all weekend. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: $30 per entry of up to 5 works. Prize: $100 Best in Photography + $100 Best in Fine Art + 3 × $50 Producers Choice + festival Artist Pass.

item.title: 27th Annual Joan L. Dunfey Open Juried Exhibition · New Hampshire Art Association
item.description: NHAA's long-running open-themed juried show at the Robert Lincoln Levy Gallery in Portsmouth, now in its 27th year, honouring Joan L. Dunfey (1925–1998), a Seacoast patron of the arts whose fund still supports artists. It is open to artists across New England working in all mediums, and the association's programme makes clear photography counts — it also runs the annual Lotte Jacobi Juried Show in the same gallery. There is no set subject: the jury is looking for strong work of any kind. Sarah Elliott, Lecturer of Painting and Drawing at the University of New Hampshire, is the juror; she trained at Boston University and worked for years in Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, China and France, and her own practice moves between figurative and non-figurative oil, watercolour and charcoal. Artists may submit one to three works, original, completed in the last three years and not previously shown at the gallery. 2D framed work is capped at 60 inches in the longest dimension including frame; freestanding 3D work at 42 inches in any dimension; wall-hung 3D over 35 pounds needs the artist's help to install. Every entry needs an image of at least 1200px on the long side plus title, medium, dimensions, year and retail price, and a short artist statement. All work must be for sale at $100 or more, with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and artists arrange their own delivery, pickup and transit insurance. Prizes go to first, second and third place plus an Artist Under 30 Award, and entry is free for anyone under 30 thanks to an anonymous donor. Non-members pay $40 to $50 depending on how many works they enter, members $20 to $30. The exhibition runs 4–29 November 2026, with acceptances out by 5pm on Friday 16 October, drop-off 1–2 November and an opening reception on 6 November, 5–8pm. — Deadline: October 7, 2026. Fee: $40–$50 (NHAA members $20–$30; free for artists under 30). Prize: Exhibition + awards.

item.title: Journey 2026 — Stirling Photography Festival Photo Book
item.description: The Stirling Photography Festival's eighth annual commemorative photo book, themed Journey — the festival calls it “a vital part of our programme and an important fundraiser”. One picture per photographer, literal or interpretative responses to the theme, and images taken in the past are welcome; anything after a first submission is excluded. Open to photographers of all ages, skill levels and abilities, on any camera or camera phone, with no stated residency requirement — the festival runs in Stirling, Scotland, and was established in 2018. Composites are allowed provided every component image is the photographer's own; work must be camera-taken and not created with AI programs, AI-altered images are discouraged, and AI tools in the editing process are “acceptable within reason”. Selection is made by the festival's creative team during October 2026, and the book is published by the end of 2026. Submit one image with your name, an optional title and a description of up to 70 words, either by email or through the Google form — the form requires a Google sign-in, so the email route is the open one. No payment is made for the images, and entering grants the festival permission to use them beyond the book, which is sold to fundraise: in the festival's exhibition in print and online, and in future PR, advertising and fundraising. Credit to the photographer is always given. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 30×30 Call Out — Annual Exhibition 2027 · Visual Arts Scotland
item.description: Visual Arts Scotland invites its members to submit small-format work for the popular 30×30 display within its 2027 Annual Exhibition in the Upper Galleries of the Royal Scottish Academy Building, Edinburgh; the exhibition runs January 8 to February 3, 2027. The 30×30 is the show's affordable section: work is offered for sale from shelves and in print racks, priced at £250 or under, with VAS taking 40% commission on sales (35% for Professional Members). Maximum two works per artist, each presented on a precisely 30×30 cm mount — the artwork itself may be smaller — made within the last two years, wrapped in clear cellophane and labelled on the back with artist name, title, medium and price. Work on paper should be on good-quality backing card; card mounts must be of professional quality; maximum thickness of the wrapped work is 2–3 mm, with no canvases on stretchers accepted. Work previously shown with VAS or at the RSA should not be submitted, and artists insure their own work. Register each piece through the linked Google Form, whose stated closing date for submissions is 27 November 2026, then post work to the VAS studio at Out of the Blue Drill Hall, Edinburgh to arrive by Friday 18 December 2026 (the form gives 22 December), or hand-deliver to the RSA upper galleries on Sunday 3 January 2027. No entry fee, and no jury: VAS lists "Guaranteed inclusion in the members 30X30 section of the Annual Exhibition" among its membership benefits, though the form notes VAS may reject work that is poorly presented or does not fit the presentation guidance. Membership is required: £40 a year for General membership, £28 for Emerging (students, recent graduates and artists under 23), with fee support for artists living with disability or receiving universal credit; VAS offers it to "artists and makers engaged in the visual arts and/or contemporary craft in Scotland". Media are not enumerated for the 30×30 itself, but the parent Annual Exhibition welcomes "all areas of visual arts and contemporary crafts, including but not limited to painting, printmaking, fine-art photography, drawing", and the 30×30 rules explicitly accommodate work on paper. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + sales.

item.title: Queens Arts Fund: New Work Grant 2027 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: A project grant of $3,000 to $7,500 for Queens-based artists to make new work — work that has not been produced or presented to an audience before. The Queens Arts Fund is administered by NYFA and supported by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs through the Greater New York Arts Development Fund, in partnership with the City Council. Photography is a named discipline: applications are sorted to peer-review panels by discipline, and Visual Arts explicitly covers Painting, Photography, Printmaking/Drawing/Book Arts and Craft/Sculpture. To apply you must live in Queens or hold a full-time studio lease there (PO boxes are not accepted), be at least 18 by 31 December 2026, and propose a project with a free or sliding-scale public component — an exhibition, screening, reading or workshop — taking place in Queens between 1 January and 31 December 2027. Artist collectives may apply through one Queens-based lead applicant. Grant funds can cover artist fees (the fund actively encourages applicants to pay themselves), technical assistance, planning and preparation, supplies and materials, venue rental for the project, in-state travel and marketing, with individual supply items capped at $1,000. The equipment line is narrower than it first looks: cameras and lighting are eligible only as equipment “related to the creation and promotion of virtual programming”, and equipment or capital goods whose total exceeds $1,000 are ineligible outright. Studio or living rent, residency fees, acquisitions, out-of-state travel and reception catering cannot be covered. Applications are scored by peer panels on four equally weighted criteria including creativity and artistic merit, and recipients may be awarded 50–100% of what they request, so the form asks for a contingency plan. Only one application to either Queens Arts Fund programme is allowed per applicant per year; non-profit organisations apply instead to the QAF Arts Access Grant. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000–$7,500.

item.title: X ROID Cologne 2027 · The Stage Gallery
item.description: The Stage Gallery's international instant art expo returns to Cologne, the city where it began as InstantCologne in 2019, after editions in Cologne, Bonn, Vienna and Basel. X ROID Cologne 2027 runs 21–23 May 2027 at the gallery's new Cologne location on Gottesweg, a three-day festival of instant photography with a Pola Walk through the city and an international gathering of instant artists. Only original instant photographs are eligible — no prints. Accepted formats are SX-70, 600, Spectra, Packfilm, Square, Wide and Mini, from Polaroid, Polaroid Originals, Impossible Project and Fuji Instax. One exhibition space holds up to 4 Polaroids (SX-70/600/Packfilm) or a maximum of 2 8x10-inch Polaroids, and artists may book multiple spaces — the fee is charged per space, so a second space doubles it. The participation fee covers professional framing of the work by the gallery (own frames by arrangement) and inclusion in the exhibition catalogue, and — a change from the Bonn edition, which took 25% — the gallery takes no sales commission at all, so artists keep 100% of any sale. Return shipping is not included. The exhibition is juried and curated by The Stage Gallery itself; no outside juror is named, and there is no cash prize. Applying is a binding commitment: the organiser states that acceptance makes the participation fee due and non-refundable even if the artist then cancels. Copyright stays with the artist throughout, with a promotional-use licence for the gallery and the catalogue. Application is by email to submissions@thestagegallery.com with the subject line “Application X roid Cologne 2027”, artist and contact details, and JPG files at 1000px on the longest side. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €170 per exhibition space (early bird, until Oct 18) / €220 from Oct 19. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Revelations · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's open call for Issue Collective #3, a publication dedicated to what emerges beneath the surface of things. The call asks what it means to reveal something today, and what appears when we look more closely, listen more carefully and move past the veil of appearances — revelation as a moment of insight, discovery or unveiling, whether an unexpected perspective, a personal truth or an overlooked aspect of reality. Entry is free and open worldwide, and the organiser lists the accepted media plainly: photography, video, digital, visual design, visual data, installation, sculpture and painting. Each artist may submit one to three works. Beyond the publication, a selection of the works chosen for it will be considered in a further selection process leading to a group exhibition to be held in 2027 in one of three Italian cities — Milan, Rome or Cagliari — which the organiser has not yet fixed. Submission is through a Google Form — the same form LoosenArt uses for the Aesthetic Dynamics call running alongside this one, with a required “Select the call of interest” dropdown that assigns your entry to this one. It asks for name, country, email, website, Instagram, an artist statement of up to 70 words in English, and up to three files of no more than 5 MB each, renamed for the work's title. LoosenArt's site is a spare Google Sites presence run from Quartu Sant'Elena in Sardinia, and beyond the call text it publishes no further terms; no charge of any kind is mentioned at any stage. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 2027 Black Creativity Juried Art Exhibition — Teen Category · Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
item.description: The teen half of Black Creativity, the longest continually running exhibition of African American art in the United States, shown at Chicago's Griffin Museum of Science and Industry since 1970 and now in its 57th year. The Teen Category is free to enter and open to Black teen artists in the Chicagoland area — within 100 miles of the museum — who are enrolled in grades 9 through 12 in the 2026/27 school year; the General Category runs alongside it for adult artists nationwide. Contemporary work in any visual medium is accepted, and the museum's own exhibition page names photography outright among the media it shows. Submit up to four works made during the last school year or since, anonymously, each original and unsold and not previously selected for a Black Creativity exhibition; a teacher or caregiver may help with the technical side but the artist submits for themselves. The same three jurors judge both categories. Teen awards are $600 for Best in Show, $375 for second place and $250 for third, and selected work hangs in the exhibition from January 18 to April 18, 2027. Accepted work must arrive framed or otherwise finished and ready to install, with delivery and pickup by the artist — 2D work may not exceed 60 inches in any direction, 3D work 30 inches, and nothing may weigh more than 50 pounds. Acceptances go out by November 4, 2026, local drop-off is December 18–19 and work is collected April 23–24, 2027. The museum does not solicit sales, but artists may sell from the walls and no commission is taken. AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $600 / $375 / $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Eye of Readers — Portfolio Submissions · L'Œil de la Photographie
item.description: Every weekend L'Œil de la Photographie — published in English as The Eye of Photography — gives an issue over to its readers, publishing a selection of portfolios sent in from around the world. The magazine publishes daily in both English and French out of Paris, and the readers' section sits alongside its regular coverage of exhibitions, festivals, books and photographers. The magazine states the section is open to amateurs and professionals alike. Submission is free and rolling: there is no deadline and no entry fee, and selected portfolios are published on the magazine's site with the artist's text and a link to their website. What is asked is a coherent series of 12 to 15 photographs and a text about the series, with a title and, if there is one, a website link; English and French versions of the text are appreciated. Files must be jpg or jpeg, at least 1350 pixels wide for horizontals and 1200 pixels high for verticals, between 150KB and 2MB each, named series-title-lastname-firstname-photonumber.jpg. The magazine is blunt that the specification is a filter in itself: any submission that does not strictly follow these guidelines will not be considered. Entries go through a JotForm the magazine links from its own guidelines page; there is no selection fee, no publication fee and no membership requirement — the paid Premium membership on the same site buys archive access to readers, and is unrelated to submitting. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Brooks International Fellowship 2027
item.description: Two six-month fellowships run jointly by Delfina Foundation and Tate, now in the programme's thirteenth year, placing international researchers inside Tate Britain's Curatorial Division from 5 April to 17 September 2027 while living in residence at Delfina Foundation in London. The two strands are separate calls with separate application forms. The first, Leonora Carrington: Art and the Theatre of Life, asks a Fellow to undertake foundational research into the British-Mexican artist's interest in theatre, performance and performativity — locating, analysing and contextualising theatrical materials across archives, manuscripts, correspondence, photographs and ephemera and situating them within Carrington's transnational career; Tate notes that a Fellow with knowledge of the Mexican social-political context and of performance histories in the second half of the twentieth century would be well placed. The second, Artist Supported Studios, contributes to research and development for the 2028 Tate Britain Commission through the lens of artists who work with supported studios — organisations that enable disabled and neurodivergent artists to sustain professional practices through long-term studio provision, advocacy and creative support — examining how collaborative artistic practices can be documented and interpreted while remaining attentive to artistic agency. The position is non-salaried, and full time: 36 hours a week for six months, broadly four days at Tate to one at Delfina Foundation. Fellows receive a research resource allowance, travel to Tate Modern, Tate Liverpool and Tate St Ives and to other UK and European institutions, a return economy flight, UK airport transfers, reimbursement of visa fees with support through the visa process, a £40 per day living allowance, a London travel pass, and a single bedroom at the Delfina house, which hosts up to eight residents around shared bathrooms, laundry, kitchen, library and dining room. Fellows get access to Tate's collection, archive, staff and networks, and opportunities to present their own practice at Tate and Delfina events. Open to international researchers based outside the UK. Applications are not made online: the relevant Word application form is downloaded from the Tate listing and emailed to Tate, with an alternative video or audio format available on request. The deadline is Wednesday 21 October 2026 at 17:00 GMT; shortlisted candidates are contacted by 30 October, two rounds of Zoom interviews run between 5 and 27 November, and successful candidates are notified by 4 December 2026. Tate asks that the words in the application be the applicant's own, warning that responses which read as generic or artificially generated could count against an application or see it rejected. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded fellowship + £40/day living allowance.

item.title: Small Wonders · St. Louis Artists' Guild
item.description: A juried exhibition built entirely around scale: every submitted work must measure 11 x 14 inches or smaller, frame included. The Guild frames it as a challenge rather than a restriction — thoughtful composition, experimentation and creative problem-solving inside a compact format, from bold statements to quiet observations. Open to all media and all subject matter, which puts photography on equal footing with painting, printmaking and sculpture, and one of the two jurors is a photographer: Zackary Petot, a multidisciplinary artist working in printmaking, photography and mixed media, and the Guild's Executive & Artistic Director. He judges alongside Kathryn Nahorski, the Guild's former Executive Director and current Development Director, who has spent fourteen years at the organisation and staged hundreds of exhibitions in professional galleries and alternative spaces. The St. Louis Artists' Guild has been running since 1886 and shows in a contemporary gallery and education space at Jackson and Forsyth in Clayton, Missouri. Entrants must be 18 or over and resident in the United States. Work must be original, completed within the last three years, and not previously shown in the Guild's galleries. One application per artist, carrying up to three works; files are JPG or PNG, maximum 1920 pixels on the longest side at 300 dpi, up to 50MB each. Wall-mounted work needs wire and screw eyes, French cleats or another professional hanging device — no saw-tooth hangers, no clip frames — and canvases must be framed or gallery-wrapped. Works must be priced for sale or marked NFS with an insurance value; the Guild insures 65% of the stated value and takes a 35% commission on sales. Accepted work can be hand-delivered or shipped via FedEx or UPS at the artist's cost. The call closes at midnight on October 31, 2026 and the exhibition runs November 20, 2026 to January 2, 2027. The Guild charges an entry fee and prints no amount on either its own call page or the visible prospectus, where EntryThingy shows only "Paid Entry"; the platform's own listing data for this call gives a floor of $10, and the exact charge is settled at checkout after creating an account. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: From $10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Omi: Artists — Australia Committee Fellowship 2027
item.description: A dedicated fellowship call for artists legally living and working in Australia, giving them a place in the 2027 Art Omi: Artists residency without competing in the general open call, which closed on September 14. The fellowship covers travel and adds a $500 stipend for material expenses on top of the residency itself. Art Omi gathers roughly two dozen international artists each summer on its campus in Ghent, in New York's Hudson Valley, two and a half hours north of New York City, for three and a half weeks of concentrated studio time balanced against cultural exchange and critical appraisal. Residents get a private bedroom in shared living quarters, a private studio and three meals a day at no cost. Two critics or curators join each session as Critics-in-Residence, leading discussions and conducting individual studio visits, while the Visitors Program brings critics, curators, gallerists and established artists to the campus; the session ends with a public Open Studios event. Facilities include indoor and protected outdoor studios, a kiln and basic hand tools, and the organiser notes that professional colour photography labs are located in nearby Ghent. Applicants must be legally resident in Australia with proof of residency, 18 or over, and must show at least ten years of demonstrated art practice on their CV — a higher bar than the five years asked of the general pool. Current BFA and MFA students are not eligible, nor are past Art Omi residents; submitted work must date from the past ten years and the application must be written in English. The residency page adds that artists eligible for this fellowship may also submit a second application to the general open call, which a separate panel reviews. Applications close September 30, 2026 at 11:59pm EST, decisions are sent January 1, 2027, and the session runs June 17 to July 12, 2027. Art Omi charges $15 to apply to its general open call, but states directly under this fellowship that the application fee for eligible artists is waived, and the fellowship's own application form prices nothing. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded residency + Travel grant + $500 stipend.

item.title: Arts to Hearts Magazine Issue 15 — WHERE I AM
item.description: The 15th edition of Arts to Hearts Magazine, published in collaboration with StudioToGallery, will feature 100 selected artists from around the world under the theme WHERE I AM — the places, experiences, memories, environments, relationships and cultures that shape an artist's perspective, including where an artist stands within their own practice. Work already made is welcome; no new work is required. The magazine takes painting, drawing and illustration, photography, sculpture, ceramics, textile and fibre art, printmaking, mixed media, collage, digital art, installation and new media, and is distributed internationally through Amazon, Barnes & Noble and other channels. Each of the 100 selected artists receives a dedicated two-page feature carrying their selected artwork, a professionally prepared interview, artist information or biography and links to their website and social platforms, plus an official certificate. From the 100, a Top 10 receive official recognition and an exclusive mentorship session with Arts to Hearts founder Charuka Arora and StudioToGallery founder Sonia Borrell; from those, a Top 3 are named Cash Award Winner, 1st Runner-Up and 2nd Runner-Up. The Cash Award Winner receives $500 plus a four-page feature, one-year StudioToGallery membership, physical trophy and certificate; both runners-up receive a two-page feature, membership, trophy and certificate. Open to artists of all genders, nationalities, backgrounds, career stages and disciplines, emerging and established. The entry fee is tiered by the number of works — $21 for 1, $35 for 3, $50 for 5, $62 for 10, $100 for 20 — and is non-refundable; an optional $27 add-on for a published artist interview is offered at checkout, and the organiser states there is no additional mandatory publication package if selected. AI-generated artwork is not eligible. Applications go through the Arts to Hearts portal; payment and final submission are separate steps. Results are expected about three weeks after the deadline. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500 + Publication.

item.title: 101 Art Book: Texture Edition · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: The fifteenth edition of the 101 Art Book, a global publishing project that brings 101 artists together around a single open theme in each volume. Texture Edition is for artists whose work is shaped by surface, material and the physical decisions of making — surfaces built by hand, found in the world, or created entirely through mark and process. Painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, fibre, printmaking, collage, found objects, paper, digital media and installation are considered on the same terms; the organiser states a strong ceramic surface competes with a strong painted one, not against a quota, and that photographers who study bark, rust, stone, fabric and weathered walls are working directly with the theme. Rachel Burke, a Meanjin/Brisbane-based multidisciplinary artist and designer, is guest curator for this edition and reviews every submission alongside the Arts to Hearts editorial team. The book is a premium hardcover distributed through the Arts to Hearts Project Shop, Amazon and Barnes & Noble, with distribution expanding into independent bookstores. Every selected artist receives a dedicated two-page spread with their work and artist profile plus an Official Certificate of Recognition. From the 101, three artists receive additional recognition: the Winner takes a $500 cash award and a four-page feature, the two runners-up a two-page feature, each of the three with a glass trophy, certificate, Arts to Hearts promotional feature and Artsy artist listing. Open worldwide to individual artists aged 18 and above, emerging to established. Copyright never transfers to the organiser, there is no publication or page fee if selected, and every applicant receives personalised jury feedback and a Certificate of Participation. The entry fee is tiered by the number of works — $21 for 1, $35 for 3, $47 for 5, $62 for 10, $100 for 20 — and is non-refundable; an optional $22 add-on for a published virtual studio visit interview is offered at checkout. AI-generated artwork is not eligible, though digitally built texture is welcome where the artist made the surface. The call closes at 11:59pm local time on 15 October; results are announced within three weeks of the deadline. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500 + Publication + 4-page feature.

item.title: Solo Exhibition November 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase from All About Photo, open theme and open to professionals and enthusiasts alike. The selected photographer receives a month-long online solo exhibition running November 1–30, 2026 across the site's home page, competition gallery and photography exhibition directory, then permanent access in the past-exhibitions archive, plus a dedicated portfolio page carrying 20 images in the Photographers Directory. The showcase also includes an in-depth interview, a special-edition newsletter, promotion across the platform's Instagram, Facebook and Twitter accounts, and international press coverage with guaranteed publication on Bored Panda, Visura and Photophiles Magazine; past winners have been picked up by outlets including The Times UK, National Geographic España, The Sun, The Daily Mail, The Eye of Photography, Digital Camera World and Compétence Photo. Work may be sold directly to buyers with no commission taken — the artist keeps 100% of the sale price. Entry is a flat $45 for a cohesive project or portfolio of 6 to 14 images; only cohesive bodies of work are published as a Solo Exhibition. Every genre is welcome, from photojournalism and street photography to fine art, landscape and portraiture. Selection is made by All About Photo founder and editor Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, on creativity and photographic quality. The competition runs from 26 September to Tuesday 20 October 2026, 11:59pm PST. Judging runs 26–31 October and the winner is notified by email shortly after 26 October. Entrants must have reached the age of majority where they live; images are submitted by creating a free profile on the site, uploading to a portfolio and applying to the call. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: pinhole · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas announces “pinhole”, a juried online photography exhibition juried by the gallery's own director Amanda Smith. Selected work is shown in the gallery's online exhibition from 1 January to 28 February 2027, with a reception on 30 January 2027 at 2pm CT and a GalleryTalk video posted in ASG Conversations. A Smith runs these calls on a rolling calendar and typically selects several dozen images for the online gallery and an accompanying exhibition catalogue, with a hardbound book of a smaller final selection; its calls are open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide working in all photographic mediums, and work previously exhibited in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. The full prospectus, including the entry fee and image limits, had not yet been published at the time of listing — check the gallery's Calls for Entry page for the entry form once the call moves across from Upcoming. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ART MAKER Issue 6 — Open Call + Cover Prize
item.description: The sixth issue of ART MAKER, an artist-run contemporary art magazine put out two to three times a year by Meg Rogers Eldredge from Northborough, Massachusetts. The theme is simply OPEN — “send us your best work, the work that you are most proud of” — and the juror is the Austrian painter and lithographer Kurt Stimmeder, who took the First Award for Art on Paper at the 2026 OSTEN Biennial in Skopje. Photography is named outright in the accepted-media list, alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, textiles, collage, printmaking, video, animation, sound, performance documentation, installation and digital work; recent work from 2022 onwards is eligible as well as new work made for the call. Each artist makes one application of three to ten images (at least three are required to be considered, and the fee tier has to match the count — submit eight images on the $16 tier and the magazine will invoice you for the difference). What selected artists get is a two-page feature in the print and digital issue with no additional publishing fee, the option to extend that to a four- or six-page interview, features on the website, newsletter and social channels, a free digital copy and discounted print copies — and, since ART MAKER posts each cycle's issue to a mailing list of more than 100 galleries and curators, a route to the people who programme shows. New this issue is a cover prize: the artist whose work is chosen for the cover of Issue 6 receives $150 to Blick art materials (or the equivalent where Blick does not trade) plus the six-page interview. Works made with AI are not considered. Applicants must be 18 or over; the call is international, and the magazine runs a small scholarship fund for artists in regions facing war, famine or severe poverty. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $16 (up to 4 images) / $24 (up to 10 images). Prize: Publication + $150 gift card (cover artist).

item.title: olio e-zine — Truth · Aesthetic Revolt Art
item.description: The first issue of olio, a new e-zine put together by the visual artist Marie Magnetic, who runs it under the name Aesthetic Revolt Art. The theme is “truth”, and the brief is deliberately wide open: the call is for “all mediums that can be digitally published”, which takes in photography alongside everything else that survives a screen. Entry is free and each artist may submit one piece, as a JPG or PNG up to 50MB. Three things are worth knowing before you spend time on it. First, this is issue one — there is no back catalogue to judge the editing or production against, so you are submitting to an unproven publication; the upside is that it costs nothing but the picture. Second, the organiser's own website carries no page for this call: the terms above come from the call record she publishes on EntryThingy, and work is accepted only through a Google Form, which is sign-in gated and so requires a Google account to fill in. Third, nothing is published about rights — the call record sets out no licence, credit or usage terms, and the form itself cannot be read without signing in — so that is worth asking about before you send work. What a contributor gets is publication in the issue; no fee, payment or prize is mentioned anywhere. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Surreal Salon 19 · Baton Rouge Gallery
item.description: The nineteenth edition of Baton Rouge Gallery's annual international exhibition celebrating pop-surrealism and lowbrow art, held in partnership with the LSU School of Art and open to artists over 18 anywhere in the world. The guest juror is Lauren YS, who hand-picks the show through a blind process — the juror sees neither the artist's name nor their home city. Judging criteria are stated as conceptual and aesthetic quality, feasibility of display, and overall artistic merit. Photography is not listed among accepted media because no media list is published; what the gallery does say is that “for more than a decade, Surreal Salon has featured paintings, photography, ceramics, textiles, mixed media works, and more.” Work must be physical, tangible and non-perishable, and two-dimensional work must arrive ready to hang in a professional gallery — no bull clips, clip frames, magnets, push-pins or poster frames. $2,000 in cash prizes is awarded: $1,000 Best in Show, $600 second, $400 third. The gallery states in one place that the Best in Show artist is profiled in an online editorial by Beautiful Bizarre Magazine and in another that the editorial runs on juxtapoz.com; the two sentences sit in the same document, so expect one of them. Entry is $35 for up to three works. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 50% commission on anything sold, which is steep and worth pricing for. Selected work is delivered by 6pm on December 19, 2026; the show runs January 2 to 24, 2027 at the gallery on Dalrymple Drive, and shipping both ways is the artist's cost. Work left uncollected after February 14, 2027 is charged $10 a day in storage. The gallery reserves the right to disqualify submissions it deems pornographic, explicitly violent, obscene or hateful. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000 / $600 / $400 cash + exhibition.

item.title: Lay of the Land: A Focus in Nature · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Artlink's juried group exhibition of work exploring the natural world, open to any artist 18 or over living in the United States. The gallery asks for artworks that engage the natural world through subject matter or materials — realistic depictions of flora and fauna, abstract interpretations of geological textures, or, in its own phrase, “the complex, evolving dialogue between humanity and the environment.” The call is explicit that it is open to all media, and it names photography and video alongside painting, ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, installation, fiber, assemblage and drawing. There is no size limit. Entry is $12 per work with a limit of ten entries, submitted online only; jury notifications go out after November 16, 2026, accepted work is delivered by December 13, 2026, and the show runs January 7 to February 7, 2027 at the gallery. Artlink is a 501(c)3 nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne, funded in part by Arts United and the Indiana Arts Commission. Accepted work must arrive ready to install and professionally presented. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: $12 per entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Adhesive Resistance · Woman Made Gallery
item.description: Woman Made Gallery's virtual juried exhibition of printed matter, open to women and non-binary artists worldwide. The call names stickers, zines, pins, buttons and other printed matter, and asks for work that embraces “experimentation, cultural commentary, humor, urgency, and the democratic spirit of DIY publishing” — polished work and beautiful roughness alike. Sticker designs may be submitted as single designs or as sheets. Photography is not named as a medium either way: what the call enumerates is object types rather than media, so a photographer's route in is the printed object — a photo zine, a sticker sheet, a small-format multiple — rather than a print on a wall. The exhibition is hosted on the gallery's own website from February 27 to March 27, 2027 and promoted across its social channels. Artists in the Chicagoland area who are selected are also invited to take part in an optional in-person pop-up print fair at the gallery, and may propose workshops or demos for in-gallery programming alongside the virtual show — those proposals, if accepted, are paid. Entries are due December 31, 2026 at 11:00 PM CST, with notification January 31, 2027. The juror is Courtney Nzeribe, a Chicago-based interdisciplinary artist and writer working across fiber, painting, printmaking, collage and mixed media, who sits on the gallery's board. The entry fee is $20 — lower than the $30 on the gallery's two other current calls and the $35 of its general terms. Woman Made offers around 30 fee waivers per juried exhibition, 15 of them reserved for ALAANA/BIPOC and/or LGBTQIA+ artists, granted on a rolling basis for financial instability or low-income status, student or recent-graduate status, or other demonstrated need; members at the Enhanced Artist level and above receive one free entry a year. The gallery welcomes art from all women, including trans women and femme/feminine-identifying genderqueer and non-binary artists. Work previously shown at Woman Made cannot be resubmitted. Submitted work must be original, created by the artist, and produced without the primary use of AI image-generation tools. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Virtual exhibition.

item.title: Cedarhurst High School Art Competition 2027
item.description: Two juried competitions for high school students, run together by Cedarhurst Center for the Arts, an AAM-accredited museum and sculpture park in Mount Vernon, Illinois. Selected work hangs in the New Semantics Gallery of the Mitchell Museum, January 24 to March 21, 2027. The Cedarhurst High School Art Competition is open to students in grades 9 to 12; the Cedarhurst Administrative Counselors Art Scholarship is a separate competition for graduating seniors, for a one-year college scholarship of $2,000 contingent on the student's formal acceptance to a university. Seniors may enter both. Eligibility is also geographic — 28 named counties: Alexander, Clay, Clinton, Edwards, Franklin, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Jackson, Jefferson, Johnson, Lawrence, Marion, Massac, Monroe, Perry, Pope, Pulaski, Randolph, Richland, Saline, St Clair, Union, Wabash, Washington, Wayne, White and Williamson. The call page words this as students in those counties, the registration form as high schools in them. The accepted-media list names “painting (oil, acrylic, watercolor), drawing, sculpture, printmaking, photograph (digital or film), pastels, textiles, ceramics, glass, metal, and wood”, with no installations; work must be original, and the organisers reserve the right to disqualify AI-generated images or work that violates copyright. Entry is normally school-mediated: a teacher registers the school, is emailed a shared Google folder and sheet for uploading JPEGs, may enter up to 25 artworks with a limit of 3 per student, and is invoiced $3 per artwork once the window closes. Seniors submit one portfolio of six works for $10. Home-school students, and anyone who wants to enter without a registered teacher, are told on the call page to contact the competition's organiser directly. Awards total more than $3,000 and are chosen after the work is delivered: the $2,000 scholarship, $200 Best of Show, $100 / $75 / $50 for first, second and third in both Best of Two-Dimensional and Best of Three-Dimensional Art, and twenty honorable mentions of $25 each. Accepted work is emailed to registered teachers by the end of December 18, 2026 and must reach the Mitchell Museum by Friday January 15, 2027; it cannot be removed before the exhibit closes, and is collected March 23 to April 2, 2027. The organiser's two surfaces disagree on the deadline and the earlier is stored: the call page requires uploads by 5pm December 2, 2026, the registration form says artwork must be registered by December 3, 2026. — Deadline: December 2, 2026. Fee: $3 per artwork ($10 per senior portfolio). Prize: $2,000 scholarship + Exhibition.

item.title: Assignment Literary Magazine — 2026 Winter Issue: Visual Art
item.description: Free visual-art submissions for the Winter 2026 issue of Assignment, the literary magazine run by Southern New Hampshire University's Master of Fine Arts in Fiction or Nonfiction program. Art is considered for the front and back covers of the issue as well as for internal use; artists may submit up to five pieces per submission, formatted one piece per page, as high-resolution images. Review is blind — the guidelines ask that no name or identifying information appear on the submission. Simultaneous submissions are accepted provided the editors are told if work is placed elsewhere, and everything submitted must be original and previously unpublished. The magazine publishes using First North American Serial Rights, after which all rights revert to the author, and states that none of its content is available for use by AI. Submitted work must be the artist's own with no AI used in its creation — a line that appears in the guidelines and again on every one of the four entry-form categories. The submission window for the issue closes November 15, 2026, across all four categories (visual art, poetry, fiction and non-fiction), and the entry route is Submittable with no fee on any category. Two things to weigh: the call asks for "visual art" and nowhere enumerates the media it accepts, so photography is not named either way — what settles it is the magazine's own record. Its online-only section ran a photographic essay, "Through Mami’s Eyes", a visual diary of the artist’s mother through the Covid-19 pandemic by Gabrielle Ghzala LaGuerre, described there as "a photo-based artist whose work explores people in their natural environments", and its Featured Artwork posts carried Guilherme Bergamini, a "Reporter photographic and visual artist" who "has developed projects with photography" — both in 2023, which is where that section stops. Neither the guidelines nor the entry form mentions payment; the stated return is publication. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Alternatives 2027 — Identity Fractured · Ohio University School of Art + Design
item.description: The 2027 edition of Alternatives, the photography biennial that Ohio University's MFA Photography + Integrated Media programme has run out of The School of Art + Design since 1980. The organisers describe it as "a long running biennial juried exhibition" that has "achieved national recognition for its leadership in forging new definitions in the medium by emphasizing the work of photographers in the conceptual forefront of the practice", and its money comes from an unusual endowment — the legacies of Clarence White, founder of the Clarence White School of Photography in New York, and his son Clarence White Jr., who re-established the school at Ohio University in 1948 and created what the programme calls the first degree-granting photography programme at a major university in the country. Past jurors named by the organisers are Carrie Mae Weems, Duane Michals, Kelli Connell, Jason Reed, Judy Natal and, most recently, Willie Osterman; the 2027 juror is Dan Estabrook. This cycle's theme is Identity Fractured: "Photography is a medium that has the power to capture, preserve, change, and distort history, places, and people. Using this medium we can tell stories about ourselves and others, play pretend, or show real pieces of ourselves... We are taking and analyzing parts of ourselves within every frame. Whether it is self portraiture, photographing others, or even objects. We all place ourselves into an image one way or another." Each artist may submit five files at 10 MB each for a flat $35, through a Google Form that requires a Google account to open. The programme gives its own address as the Ohio University Art Gallery in Athens; the 2027 call itself names no venue. Two disclosures: the School of Art + Design's own Alternatives page had not been updated at the time of listing and still carries the 2025 edition ("Image as Record", juried by Willie Osterman), so the 2027 call lives on the programme's own Instagram and on the submission form; and while previous editions were billed as an international biennial, the 2027 poster reads "A National Photography Biennial" — no residency or nationality rule is published on either surface. Neither readable surface announces a notification date, prize money or exhibition dates, and the entry form is sign-in gated, so it could not be read. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 ArtFields Competition & Festival
item.description: ArtFields turns the whole of Lake City, South Carolina into a gallery for seventeen days each spring, and its signature visual-art competition is open for the 2027 edition — the festival's 15th year. Work is not hung on white walls: selected pieces go up in "galleries, warehouses, restaurants, shops, and other venues throughout downtown," so that, as ArtFields puts it, art is met "from grabbing their cup of morning coffee to getting a haircut." An average of 400 works are invited from the submissions, rated 1–10 by an independent panel of arts professionals through the ArtBooth platform. Photography is unambiguously in: the competition rules say "Artists may submit one 2-D or 3-D artwork in any visual art medium," and the entry portal repeats that the competition "is open to artists of all media." The prize pool is over $100,000 — a $50,000 Grand Prize and a $25,000 Second Place chosen by the jury panel, two $12,500 People's Choice Awards (one 2-D, one 3-D) decided by public vote, five $2,000 Merit Awards, and Southeastern Partnership Awards of exhibitions and opportunities. An artist may win only one of the top four. The entry is $25 for a single work; you may upload up to five images of that one work, and submitting a portfolio of separate pieces is grounds for disqualification. Eligibility is regional and strict: you must have lived in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia or West Virginia for at least six consecutive months before submitting, be 18 or older, and the work must have been completed in or after 2024. Work shown at a previous ArtFields is not eligible, and last year's top-four winners sit out a cycle. Submissions close 11:59 p.m. EDT on Sunday, November 1, 2026; invitations and declines go out by Wednesday, December 9, 2026; venue invitations follow by January 29, 2027 and the signed Artist & Venue Hosting Agreement is due February 5. Work must reach Lake City between March 5 and 13, 2027 (installations by March 20) and stay up for the festival, 9 April – 1 May 2027; artists other than installation-makers need not travel, as trained handlers install at each venue. Costs to weigh: you pay transport both ways and insure the work yourself, return shipping requires a prepaid label packed with the piece, and venues take 20% of any sale. Work is sold at the artist's discretion, and top-four winners agree to leave the awarded piece with ArtFields / the Lake City Creative Alliance for a further 90-day public exhibition, during which ArtFields has an option — not an obligation — to acquire it for its permanent collection, with the cash award as the full and only consideration. One technical rule worth reading twice: work "deemed not ready to hang or show as delivered will be excluded," so D-rings and wiring matter. ArtFields also bars anything "created solely through Artificial Intelligence (AI) software." — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $50,000 / $25,000 / 2 × $12,500 + 5 × $2,000.

item.title: Future Visions · Kunsthalle Luzern
item.description: Kunsthalle Luzern and the akku Kunstplattform in Emmenbrücke have launched a Switzerland-wide open call on a single question: what does the future look like from here? "The future is not a place we wait for," the call opens. "It takes shape in the images, conflicts and decisions of the present." The two institutions are after work that engages social, technological, ecological or political transformation and builds an independent position out of it — "conceptual, speculative, poetic, critical or experimental approaches from all areas of contemporary" art. It is free to enter and open to artists resident in Switzerland, individuals and collectives alike, from students to established practitioners; existing works and newly planned projects are equally welcome, provided a proposal is "technically and spatially feasible" within what the two spaces can do. Submit at least one and at most three proposed works, each with title, year, material, dimensions and up to five images (video as a link plus a still — no uploaded files), all inside one PDF of 10 MB or less named Surname_Firstname_FV2027.pdf. You cannot apply to just one of the two venues: a single proposal may be assigned to only one of them, but different proposals from the same practice can go to both, and site-specific proposals are the one exception, provided the tie to that space is argued in the application. Selection is by the curatorial teams of both institutions together with three external experts — Katrin Sperry, Michel Rebosura and Sebastian Utzni — on artistic and conceptual quality, thematic relevance, willingness to experiment, and feasibility. Two separate exhibitions follow: Kunsthalle Luzern 4 July – 19 September 2027 (opening Saturday 3 July), akku Kunstplattform 11 July – 5 September 2027 (opening Saturday 10 July). On money, the institutions commit in writing: "The Kunsthalle Luzern and the akku Kunstplattform are committed to fair fees and good working conditions for artists. Exhibition fees are based on the visarte recommendations applicable to smaller institutions," with further contributions towards production costs possible in justified cases from the project budget — no figure is published. Artists pay transport and return themselves; the institutions insure the work from receipt through dismantling, and artists supply their own monitors, projectors and playback equipment for media works. Applications go only through the form on the Kunsthalle Luzern project page — nothing else is accepted — and close Sunday 15 November 2026, with jury feedback by Monday 14 December 2026. The project was conceived by Marius Geschinske, director of the Kunsthalle Luzern. Neither the project page nor the six-page open-call dossier names a medium list beyond "all areas of contemporary art"; the Kunsthalle's group show *Crossroad – Home in Motion* (4 July – 27 September 2026) put photographers among its sixteen positions — Hans U. Alder, whose own site is fotografiealder.com, and Mischa Christen, "a Swiss photographer based in Lucerne". — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Artist fee.

item.title: Fins, Feathers, and Fur · St. Charles Arts Council
item.description: "Beyond the surface of animal portraiture lies a rich world of pattern, rhythm, and tactile wonder." The St. Charles Arts Council's juried autumn show asks for work that investigates the physical and visual surfaces of the animal kingdom — "literal representations, or abstract explorations" — under the subtitle *Textures of the Living World*. It hangs in the council's SCAC Gallery at 121 2nd Street in historic downtown St. Charles, Illinois, from 30 October to 20 December 2026, with awards handed out at the opening reception on Friday 30 October, 5–7pm. All media are accepted — the organiser says so twice, "All mediums are accepted, 3d encouraged" and "All forms of media accepted" — so photographs compete alongside everything else; the judge is Chris Hughes, an award-winning member of Oil Painters of America who sits on the boards of the Naperville Art League and the DuPage Art League and teaches at both. Awards are Best in Show $150, second place $75, third place $50, plus honourable mentions at the judge's discretion. Entry is $35 for non-members and $20 for SCAC members, selected from a drop-down at checkout, and one entry covers up to two pieces; only one entry per artist. Work must be original, created within the last five years, and must not have been shown in any previous SCAC exhibit. Everything must be for sale — the council is explicit that the "NFS" option in the entry form must not be selected — and sales split 60% to the artist, 40% to the council. Two practical constraints before you enter: all work must be wired to hang, with sawtooth hangers refused, and you must be able to make the in-person dates yourself, drop-off Monday 26 October 2–6pm and collection Monday 21 December 2–6pm, which effectively limits this to artists who can get to St. Charles twice. Two clauses of the artist contract are worth reading before you pay: all artists with work in the show "are asked to sign up to volunteer at The ARC" on two-hour shifts, and any work not claimed within seven days of the pick-up date, without notice, "becomes the property of the St. Charles Arts Council". Entries close 11 October 2026 and the jury decision is posted 14 October. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $35 non-members / $20 SCAC members. Prize: $150 / $75 / $50 + Exhibition.

item.title: Embodied Existence · Chronic Pain Project
item.description: The Chronic Pain Project is a 501(c)(3) built on a simple premise — "Chronic pain is invisible. We can change that" — that brings artists living with chronic pain together so their work can do the explaining. Its next exhibition, *Embodied Existence*, asks what it means to be embodied while living with chronic pain, and it hangs at the Watzek Library on the Lewis & Clark College campus in Portland from 9 October to 6 November 2026. Entry is free and the bar is deliberately low: "Art depicting the experience of living with chronic pain. That's it. No specific medium, style, or approach required. Just your truth, told your way." All skill levels are welcome — "You don't need formal training or a gallery resume" — 2D and 3D work are both encouraged, though display space for 3D is limited, and photography sits comfortably inside that. There is a content screen, though: the project does not accept explicit content — "Keep it PG-13 - no drugs, sex, alcohol" — and work "will be turned away if it contains discriminatory themes and gratuitous violence", which is worth weighing if your account of chronic pain runs through medication. Who may enter: anyone 18 or over who lives with chronic pain, or who cares for someone who does. Caregivers are actively wanted and the definition is broad — healthcare providers, family, friends, community members — with the one condition that a caregiver's submission be health-related in some way. The call is local by design: only work that can be dropped off on 8 October and collected on 9 November at the Lewis & Clark campus is accepted, so this is for the Portland metropolitan area. Two submissions per artist are allowed and roughly 10–15 further pieces will fit in the show, so both may not be taken. Work must arrive exhibition-ready and installation-ready — hanging hardware attached, since "work that arrives without proper installation hardware cannot be included" — and the project handles installation at the venue. Nothing is insured: the terms warn that work "may be installed in high-traffic locations or other places with public access and little or no supervision" with "minor theft deterrent elements", and that neither the project nor the exhibition site carries coverage against damage, destruction or theft, so that risk stays with the artist. You upload at least two good photographs of the piece and a short statement; submit through Artwork Archive and also complete the project's Google Form, since both are required. Work will be for sale at the exhibition and in the project's online gallery, with the artist keeping 75% and the project 25%. Artists are optionally invited to record a video about the work for the project's artist-interview series. The deadline is Friday 2 October 2026 and acceptances are confirmed by 6 October. One inconsistency to note: the project's own Upcoming Events page lists the Watzek Library exhibit as running 5 October 2026 – 5 January 2027, while the call document and the entry platform both say 9 October – 6 November; the call's own dates are used here. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Yéego Action Grant · First Peoples Fund
item.description: First Peoples Fund's Yéego Action Grant exists for the moment a working artist needs money quickly and there is no cycle to wait for. It offers $100 to $2,500 to individual Native artists and culture bearers who need "financial assistance with a specific professional opportunity or towards a hardship that is hindering their creative practice." The name carries the Diné word *yéego*, a phrase of encouragement that can mean "keep going" or "don't give up." The eligible uses are concrete and unusually practical: entry or workshop fees to take up an art opportunity; travel, lodging and meals to attend a residency, seminar or similar professional development; expenses from an emergency such as fire, theft or a natural disaster; repair of damaged equipment or tools; unanticipated transport needs, from a vehicle repair to a bus pass; unexpected medical or health costs that stop you working; and sudden unforeseen expenses on a current project, such as replacing damaged supplies or finding a new venue. What it will not do is equally clear — no reimbursement for money already spent, no general purchases of new tools, materials or equipment, no tuition or student loans, no organisational operating support, and no funding for new or existing projects, exhibitions or programming. Applicants must be at least 18, must be enrolled members of or provide proof of lineal descent from a US federally or state-recognised tribe, or proof of Alaska Native or Native Hawaiian ancestry, must be practising artists, must not be enrolled in a degree-seeking programme, and must not have received a Yéego grant before; current FPF grantees, fellows and leaders of grantees are ineligible, and group or multiple-artist requests are not considered. The Submittable application adds one bar the programme page omits: an applicant "must be a U.S. based resident". There is no fee. Applications run through Submittable and ask for three recent examples of your work with a brief description of each, used to confirm you are a practising artist; a website or social link is optional and explicitly does not affect scoring, because FPF "recognise[s] that not everyone maintains an online presence." Supporting links and up to two documents — an invoice, a quote, a budget — are also optional. The grant runs on a monthly rhythm: the portal normally opens by the 12th, the deadline is the 10th of every month at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time, applicants hear by the last day of the month, and approved funds arrive roughly six to eight weeks after the monthly due date. The round open at the time of writing closes Saturday 10 October 2026. FPF staff and leadership review the applications. One thing to know before applying: the fund is open to artists of every discipline and First Peoples Fund's own pages enumerate no list of accepted media, so nothing here is specific to photography — but nothing excludes it either, and camera repair and market entry fees are named uses. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: $100–$2,500.

item.title: Visual Art Open Call · The Closed Eye Open
item.description: The Closed Eye Open is a small art-and-literature journal — its current issue is Issue XV — that describes itself as "an exploration of the many forms of self-expression" and sets out to publish work "that may not necessarily connect with other publications" — "Pieces that are weird, unconventional, or even experimental may very well fit with what we're going for." Its visual-art call is open for upcoming issues, and photography is named in the accepted forms: "Visual art may include painting, drawing, photography & print-making, digital art, and hybrid forms." Submit up to six pieces as JPEGs at whatever file size suits you — higher resolution is requested later if a piece is taken — with a statement or cover letter, a short third-person bio, links, and optionally a title list as you want it to appear. Each piece is generally viewed individually, so a submission may deliberately vary in style and subject; if you would rather it be read as one body of work, say so in the cover letter. Simultaneous submissions are accepted on the condition that you withdraw anything placed elsewhere, and work posted only on your own website, blog or social account does not count as previously published. Rights are light-touch: acceptance grants the journal online publishing and archival rights, and after publication all rights revert to the artist, with a request for a credit if the work appears elsewhere later. Issues come out online as PDFs, two or three a year, alongside an ongoing *Maya's Micros* feature updated roughly twice a month. The editors invite people from outside the art world as much as inside — "from established writers & artists, to those in academic disciplines, to those who may be new to the world of sharing their work with a larger audience" — and say a scientific, spiritual or liberal-arts starting point is equally welcome. Submissions run through Submittable and carry a $4.50 fee; the visual-art category closes 30 September 2026. No payment to contributors is mentioned and the journal names no notification date. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $4.50. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Guest Room: Sofia Krysiak & Jack Latham · Der Greif
item.description: The next edition of Der Greif's monthly Guest Room, the Munich non-profit's online exhibition format in which an invited figure from contemporary photography curates an open submission in real time. This round is curated by Sofia Krysiak and Jack Latham, co-founders of the Nashville photobook publisher Terrible Baby, under the theme "Difficult Conversations". Their brief opens on a question — "Some conversations are difficult to have, so, how do we have them?" — and asks for work that opens up social, political or personal realities and "stories that refuse to be avoided and brushed under the carpet". The curators are explicit that photographs do not simply make hard subjects legible: images "can expose and conceal, humanise and stereotype, complicate and flatten", and the same photograph produces radically different readings depending on who is looking, who made it and where it circulates. At a moment when disagreement increasingly impedes conversation and information proliferates faster than its veracity can be gauged, they ask whether visual language can help us have the conversations we need to have. A submission is one project of one to five photographs; video works are also accepted, up to ten minutes, and if selected the full video is published on Der Greif's site with excerpts on its social channels. Entry is free — Der Greif is a registered non-profit and suggests a voluntary €5 or €10 donation, with a 50 or 100 percent discount code available by email to anyone unable to contribute. Images already selected for a past Der Greif opportunity may not be resubmitted. Selected work is published in an online showcase alongside emerging artists worldwide, and the selected photographers get an online feedback session with the curators. Krysiak is a publisher, curator, writer and photography researcher, originally from Buenos Aires and now based in Nashville, who directs Terrible Baby and co-founded HER Photo Agency; Latham is a Welsh photographer and publisher, an Associate Professor of Photography at Belmont University, whose work sits between photojournalism and conceptual art and questions the mechanisms of disinformation. The Guest Room goes live on dergreif.org on 20 November 2026. — Deadline: October 28, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €5 or €10 donation). Prize: Publication + portfolio feedback.

item.title: 2027 Artist Residencies · Djerassi Resident Artists Program
item.description: The Djerassi Resident Artists Program's 2027 season, on a 583-acre ranch in the Santa Cruz Mountains above Woodside, California, where the programme has given more than 2,700 writers, visual and media artists, composers, choreographers, filmmakers and scientists a month of time and space across 43 years — "all at no cost to the artists". Applicants pick one category per cycle, and Visual Arts is defined as "Painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, mixed media, and installation"; the programme's own 2027 details PDF credits its illustrations to "Film photography by Jessie Barr, 2025 Djerassi Program Alumnus". Five one-month sessions run from mid-February to mid-November 2027 — 16 February to 16 March, 30 March to 27 April, 22 June to 27 July (the Leonardo@Djerassi cohort of five artists and five scientists, with Leonardo/ISAST, which includes public forums, a feature in LEONARDO from MIT Press and open studios), 17 August to 14 September, and 19 October to 16 November — and the programme anticipates accommodating around 40 to 45 new artists. Each resident gets a private live/work studio with a workspace suited to their discipline, chef-prepared weeknight dinners with kitchens stocked for the rest, laundry, SFO pickup and return and local transport during the stay, and 583 acres of trails, redwoods and site-specific sculpture; artists pay their own way to the Bay Area. It is open to national and international applicants at every career stage, eligibility has recently been expanded to include degree-seeking students, alumni must wait five seasons before reapplying, and all materials must be in English. No accommodation is available for partners, children or pets, and residents commit to the whole session — there are no partial residencies. Apply through SlideRoom with a statement of interest, descriptions of two recent projects, a CV, one to five work samples (visual artists upload up to five JPEGs), your website and Instagram, and ranked session preferences. The application fee is $35. Staff screen for completeness, then a jury of artists and arts professionals scores merit of past work, readiness to engage with a month of uninterrupted time, and potential for impact; all applicants are tentatively notified by 31 December 2026. Applications opened 1 September and close 9 October 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: One-month residency.

item.title: 2027 AIM Fellowship · The Bronx Museum
item.description: The 47th cycle of the AIM Fellowship, The Bronx Museum's career accelerator for emerging artists based in New York City, founded in 1980 as Artist in the Marketplace. Fourteen artists are selected each year through open competition for a nine-month practicum of expert-led seminars at the museum: the art market, the artist statement, community building, communication strategies, the curator/artist relationship, financial literacy, funding opportunities and art law in the first half; studio visits, portfolio reviews, peer-led sessions, guest artist visits, career planning, exhibition preparation and time management, working with institutions big and small, audience development, community art practice, artist archives and documentation in the second. Fellows meet on Tuesday evenings, 6 to 9pm, at the museum from February to June 2027, break for July and August, and resume from September to December; the cohort then designs and co-facilitates a mandatory public AIM Convening in winter or spring 2028, and a group exhibition with a fully illustrated catalogue follows roughly every two years. There is no application fee and no cost to participate. AIM has helped more than 1,300 New York artists establish careers, among them Njideka Akunyili-Crosby, Glenn Ligon, Abigail DeVille, Byron Kim, Lucia Hierro, Jacolby Satterwhite and the photographer LaToya Ruby Frazier — the call names no accepted-media list at all, and that alumni roster is where the question of photography is answered. Eligibility is specific: at least 21; applying as an individual, not a partnership or collective; an emerging artist with two to ten years actively creating and presenting new original work in the visual arts who has yet to be substantially celebrated; a New York City resident at application and throughout the term; not enrolled in a degree-granting programme or another professional-development programme during the fellowship; not a Bronx Museum employee or a board member's relative; and not represented by a commercial gallery anywhere in or outside the US. Because stipends, honoraria and wage payments are involved, enrolment is limited to US citizens and permanent residents. Apply through Submittable with six works no more than three years old; semi-finalists must be available for an in-person group interview with the selection committee at the museum in autumn 2026. The museum is explicit that this is not a studio programme and that no studio space is provided. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fellowship.

item.title: Art x Newlab Creative Residency 2027 · Michigan Central
item.description: The fourth year of the Michigan Central Art x Newlab Creative Residency, a twelve-week research-based fellowship in Detroit's innovation district run in partnership with Newlab and Henry Ford Health with funds from the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation. Fellows are selected across two tracks: Art & Tech, with Newlab and Knight Foundation support, for practices at the edge of technology, data visualisation, wearable tech, accessibility and sustainability; and Art & Health, with Henry Ford Health, for artists working across wellness, care and health technology. Each fellow-in-residence receives a $30,000 prize to advance their project, access to Newlab Detroit's fabrication shops and to facilities across Michigan Central and Henry Ford Health, project-aligned research opportunities, a place in a public conversation series, and external mentors who both support the selection review and give ongoing guidance. Two sessions frame the on-site time and applicants rank a preference: 8 February to 30 April 2027, and 17 May to 6 August 2027. Michigan Central's art-programme page describes the residency as foregrounding emerging and mid-career artists based primarily in metro Detroit, and the form asks whether you are a current resident of south-eastern Michigan, but the call invites artists, creatives, researchers and makers "across disciplines and geographies"; the stated requirements are to be over 25, to apply as a single person or entity rather than a group or collaboration, and to be eligible to receive taxable income via an SSN, ITIN or EIN.
