Photography is one of the seven categories the organiser lists on its own Artwork Archive posting, alongside craft, drawing, film/video/new media, mixed media, painting and sculpture. Applying is free through Michigan Central's Submittable and the organiser has deliberately shortened it, suggesting no more than five hours in total: a project title, a one-sentence and a two-paragraph description with goals, community engagement and expected outcomes, a focus-area paragraph, a needs paragraph on equipment and technical assistance, a high-level budget for the $30,000, and up to five work samples with credit lines. A panel of experts across art, technology and health scores clarity and originality of the idea, alignment with the track themes, feasibility within twelve weeks, and potential for impact and innovation. Past fellows-in-residence include Simon Anton, Ash Arder, Michael Candy, Osman Khan, Salam Rida, Wes Taylor, Sabrina Nelson and Chloe Pascal Crawford. A virtual open house runs on 8 October 2026, and accessibility needs can be raised with the residency team. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30,000 + Residency.

item.title: 2026 Velocity Fund Project Grants
item.description: The Velocity Fund's 2026 cycle, open from 22 September to 22 November 2026, giving Philadelphia-based artists project grants of $5,000 each. It is one of 41 Regional Regranting Programs of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, hosted by Asian Arts Initiative in Philadelphia's Chinatown North after earlier stints at Philadelphia Contemporary and at Temple Contemporary in the Tyler School of Art and Architecture; the Foundation set the programme up in 2007 to reach independently organised, public-facing, artist-centred activity that animates local art scenes but lies beyond the reach of traditional funding. Applying is free — "There is no application fee to apply." Individual artists living in Philadelphia may apply, as may artist-run spaces and collectives whose lead applicant lives in Philadelphia; incorporated 501(c)(3) nonprofits, for-profit businesses, artists living outside Philadelphia, senior Asian Arts Initiative staff and any lead applicant who received a Velocity grant the previous year may not. The project must involve visual arts components, take place between February 2027 and February 2028, and reach a public outcome in Philadelphia inside that window. The fund will not reimburse or resolve work already underway, and says plainly that applications only for travel, studio rent or equipment, with no public outcome, are not encouraged; it favours projects rooted in their communities, led by artists, mindful of their impact, and staged in those communities rather than in commercial galleries and museums. The fund defines what it supports as work using visual arts "including (but never limited to) printmaking, performance, video, puppetry, sculpture, and curation" — photography is not on that list and does not need to be, since the most recent cohort includes Uriah Bussey's Disabling the Queer Lens, a film and digital photography series of Black and Brown queer disabled people made with COVID-safer portraits, ending in a photobook, cyanotype prints and a public exhibition. Apply through Submittable with a biography of the lead applicant and collaborators, a description of your audience, a description of the visual arts involved, a project proposal in writing or on video, a timeline, the fund's budget form and five to ten work samples; a lead applicant may submit one proposal per cycle, and may reuse last year's application because each year has a new panel. That panel is independent of Velocity, Asian Arts Initiative and Warhol Foundation staff, includes one former grantee and one administrator from another Regional Regranting Program, scores on artistic vision, connection to publics, capacity to realise the project and personal impact, then meets over the 30 top-scoring applications to choose the final 12 to 14 grantees; the panellists are named after the awards are made. Grantees are notified in early February 2027 and receive 80 percent of the money up front, the rest after a midterm check-in. Applications are also offered in Vietnamese. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 (12–14 grants).

item.title: 40th Annual Sears Invitational Art Show & Sale · Sears Art Museum
item.description: The 40th Annual Sears Invitational Art Show & Sale at the Sears Art Museum, Utah Tech University in St. George — the museum's premier event, founded by Robert N. Sears (1915–1995), a retired vice-president of Phillips Petroleum who worked to establish a quality art invitational at the university, and now one of Utah's longest-running and most popular juried museum exhibitions. Around 100 artists and roughly 200 works are selected by jury for a six-week run, 13 February to 27 March 2027, opening with a gala on 12 February. Entry is free: "There is no fee to enter!" The museum answers the media question outright in its own FAQ — "We welcome visual art of all subjects and mediums—including watercolor, oil, acrylic, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, photography, mixed media, 2D digital art, and more." Any artist aged 18 or older based in the western United States may submit, with priority given to artists from Utah, Idaho, Colorado and Nevada. You may submit up to three individual pieces, each as a separate ArtCall entry and each editable until the call closes, and a maximum of two will be accepted; recent work is asked for and everything submitted must be available for sale. Each entry needs a high-quality image, the title, dimensions, sale price and medium, your location and a brief artist bio. Selected artists are included in a professionally designed full-colour exhibition catalogue available for purchase by museum patrons, and gain the show's audience of collectors, curators, visitors and fellow artists. Sales split 60 percent to the artist and 40 percent to the museum, which funds exhibitions, educational programmes and part-time student positions, and the museum's share is tax-deductible for the buyer. Local artists drop off and collect in St. George, and the museum runs a complimentary van service to and from Ogden, Salt Lake City and Orem; artists outside Utah, or unable to use those points, are responsible for round-trip shipping. Acceptances are posted at searsart.com and emailed on 16 November 2026. One caution: one FAQ answer dates the run "February 13 through March 27, 2026" while the call's own timeline block and the ArtCall prospectus both say 2027 — the exhibition is in 2027. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Young Photographer Awards 2026 · Photo Museum Ireland
item.description: Photo Museum Ireland, the national centre for contemporary photography, runs the Young Photographer Awards as its national photography awards for young people, and the 2026 edition is open to anyone aged 8 to 18 living on the island of Ireland. The museum's own terms scope it to young people resident in the Republic of Ireland or Northern Ireland who were aged between 8 and 18 inclusive on 31 December 2025 — born between 1 January 2007 and 31 December 2017 — and entries are judged separately in two age groups, 8–13 and 14–18. Entry is free, each entrant may submit up to ten photographs, and the museum is explicit that no previous experience or specialist equipment is needed: photographs made with a phone, a digital camera, an analogue camera or another photographic process are all accepted. Judging is on three equally weighted criteria — strength of the idea, creativity and originality, and visual impact — with the photographer's age taken into account; judges see the photographs, titles and age group only, not names or contact details. One overall Young Photographer of the Year is selected from the six age-category winners, with three Rising Stars winners drawn from the 8–13 group, three from the 14–18 group, and a wider shortlist of Highly Commended photographers. Winning and shortlisted photographs go into a large-scale public outdoor exhibition on Admiral Browne Walk at Sir John Rogerson's Quay in Grand Canal Dock, Dublin, presented with support from IPUT and launching in late November 2026. Entrants under 16 need a parent or guardian to authorise the entry through a secure email link before it reaches the judges, and an unauthorised entry is deleted after seven days. Images containing elements produced or modified with artificial intelligence must be identified and categorised as such at entry, and entrants must not present AI-generated material as wholly their own photographic work. Submissions open on Monday 31 August 2026 and close at 11pm on Sunday 11 October 2026, Irish time, through the museum's CameraComp entry portal. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Rawhead: Point Blank — Semi-monthly Digital Series
item.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of poetry, fiction, nonfiction and visual art that reads the arts as a form of resistance, and Point Blank is its rapid-response strand: a digital series featuring the work of a single writer or artist, released semi-monthly, made in direct response to what is happening now. The editors describe it as a form of resistance and documentation — a way of marking what is being done, who it is being done to, and how it is being fought — and they name the ground explicitly: state violence, the kidnapping and murder of neighbours by ICE, the genocide of the Palestinian people, the plunder of the earth, economic hardship, legislative attacks on LGBTQ+ people and systemic racism. Just as explicitly, they want the other half of the ledger: mutual aid, community care, healing and recovery, the defence of neighbours, everyday kindness, and the art made in spite of it all. They say they want to hear from anyone paying attention, whether that perspective comes from the shop floor, the classroom, the kitchen table, the picket line, the waiting room, the cell, the back roads or the street. Photographers enter through the Visual Art category, which takes three to ten pieces in any medium and enumerates photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture; images should be at least 1500px as JPG, PNG or TIFF. Submission is free and the journal states it is committed to always offering free submissions, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that it says have no bearing on editorial decisions. Each featured contributor receives a flat $30 honorarium plus a $10 donation to a charity of their choice. Work not selected for Point Blank may still be considered for Rawhead's general issues. Simultaneous submissions are accepted and previously published work is welcome where the rights have reverted, the original publication is credited and at least six months have passed. AI-generated content is not accepted: submissions must be original, human-made and free of AI assistance. The editors aim to respond within three months. Rawhead's own submissions page describes Point Blank as an ongoing, semi-monthly series and gives no closing date; the dated surface is the Submittable category, whose header reads “Ends on Sun, Nov 1, 2026 4:00 AM” — that is the raw UTC instant, which is midnight US Eastern at the end of Saturday 31 October 2026. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $30 + Publication.

item.title: Anything but…Plastic · Riverside Arts Center
item.description: Riverside Arts Center, a 501(c)(3) arts centre on Huron Street in Ypsilanti, programmes Anything but…Plastic into its 2026–27 gallery season as a group exhibition built around a single material constraint. The call opens with the dictionary definition of plastic and then throws it out: no acrylic paint or gesso, no synthetic fibres, no found objects containing plastic, no Mod Podge or plastic adhesives, no 3D printing, no plastic or acrylic beads. 'Acrylic paint? Get outta here! Try some homemade egg tempera! Nylon thread? No way!' The centre's allowed list is oil paint, watercolour, natural fibres, wood, charcoal, oil pastels, ceramics and glass, and it is explicitly non-exhaustive — 'include, but are not limited to' — with an invitation to get in touch if you are unsure about your medium. Photography is not named in either list, so read the constraint as the brief rather than as a bar: a resin-coated print is polyethylene-coated and will not clear it, and an inkjet paper with a polymer receiving layer is exactly the case the gallery asks you to raise with it, while fibre-based silver gelatin, cyanotype, platinum-palladium, salted paper and other plastic-free processes plainly can. The ban is scoped to the work itself — the prospectus adds that frames and installation materials are not included — and the gallery's concurrent exhibition Deconstruction is described in its own words as combining photography, drawing, painting and found-object art. Entry is free — the centre states on its Artist Opportunities page that all of its calls for art are always free to enter — and the call is open to artists of all ages, locally, regionally and nationally, with priority possibly given to artists based in south-eastern Michigan. Applications go through Artwork Archive, which caps a submission at three pieces; the prospectus asks for one to five high-quality images plus an artist statement of 100–300 words and a one-to-two-page bio or CV. Work must be display-ready, framed or wired, and no larger than 36 by 48 inches unless pre-approved. Work created wholly or partially with AI tools must be disclosed at submission and will then be judged on the same criteria as everything else. The gallery insures work on its premises to $5,000 a piece and takes a 30 percent commission on sales; artists deliver and collect their own work at their own cost. No juror is named and no award is offered: the gallery has final authority over inclusion, and what a selected artist gets is the exhibition itself. The call closes 9 November 2026 at 11:59pm Eastern, artists are notified on 13 November, work is dropped off on 30 November, and the exhibition runs 4 December 2026 to 10 January 2027 with an opening reception on 4 December. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 BAXTER ST Residency
item.description: Baxter St at the Camera Club of New York — one of the city's oldest not-for-profit arts organisations and a base for the contemporary lens-based community — invites emerging lens-based artists living in New York City who have yet to have a solo exhibition in the city to apply for its workspace residency. Residents get free use of Baxter St's facilities and equipment for the duration of the residency, a stipend of $1,000 a month across the three months of workspace access, a $750 materials fee towards film, printing and other production costs, a $3,000 production fee to realise the exhibition, and $165 per public programme. Each resident is granted a solo exhibition at Baxter St after their residency term, and takes part in the organisation's programming: a public conversation, a video interview and one-on-one meetings with an Art Advisory Committee member and Baxter St staff. The organisers read lens-based broadly — photographers, filmmakers, collage artists and others who use photography as a medium or a point of departure are all welcome. Applicants must be New York City residents for the duration of the residency period and 18 or older; living accommodation is not provided. Only lens-based work is considered, and Baxter St staff, board members, previous Workspace or Darkroom residents and their families are not eligible. Anyone enrolled in a degree-granting programme as of 1 January 2026 is ineligible, and students must have completed their studies on or before 1 January 2027. There is no fee to apply. The application, made through Submittable, asks for a work sample of ten images (installation shots allowed) plus up to one video of a maximum three minutes, a letter of intent of up to 300 words carrying an exhibition proposal, a one-paragraph artist statement of up to 300 words, a one-page CV and two references. The 2027 application cycle opened on 23 September 2026 and closes 25 November 2026 at 11:59pm ET; Baxter St states the deadline will not be extended, and a jury of art professionals considers every eligible application. The residency is supported by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, the Joy of Giving Something, Inc., and the Howard and Sarah D. Solomon Foundation. Note on access: the ground-floor galleries and restroom at 154 Ludlow Street are wheelchair accessible, but the main resident workspace is one flight down and is not. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + $1,000/month stipend + solo exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Portrait
item.description: The SE Center's open call on the portrait, classic to contemporary. The organisers frame it around what portraits are for: objects of remembrance and reverence, of seduction and glorification — from the keepsake in a locket to the likeness of a leader meant to inspire, images that can stir and confront and drive us to action just as they can lull us into longing for a time since passed, acting as a mirror in which we find our own inward experience or as a window onto the virtues of another. Analog and digital manipulation in all its forms is welcome, monochrome or colour, any subject, analog, digital or antique processes, and photographers of every skill level and location may enter. The juror is Aline Smithson, the Los Angeles visual artist, educator and editor best known for conceptual portraiture that uses humour and pathos to explore the performative potential of photography; she has had over forty solo shows at institutions including the Griffin Museum of Photography, the Santa Barbara Museum of Art and the Center for Fine Art Photography, her work is held in public collections, and in 2007 she founded Lenscratch. Between thirty-five and forty selected images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $35 for up to five images and $6 for each additional image to a maximum of fifteen; members pay $28 and $5. Work exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years is not eligible, and there are no refunds for images not selected. The Center takes no commission — the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. Submissions opened 6 September 2026 and close 15 November; selections are announced 1 December and the exhibition runs 15 December 2026 to 30 January 2027. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35/5 images ($28 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Members Show 2026–27
item.description: The SE Center's annual members' exhibition, open to any photographer who joins the Center. Anything goes: all subjects, any photo-based imagery, analog and digital manipulation in all its forms, monochrome or colour, analog, digital or antique processes, and member photographers of every skill level and location are welcome. The juror is Michael Pannier, an award-winning fine art and commercial photographer based in Greenville with thirty years in photography and forty-five in the gallery and art world, who founded the SE Center for Photography as an exhibition and education venue after relocating from Maryland; he is represented in galleries across the United States and works regularly as an exhibition juror, curator, portfolio reviewer and speaker on the business of fine art photography. Between forty and fifty selected images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $5 per image and you may submit up to fifteen. Membership is bought directly from the Center and is not itself juried: $25 a year for secondary-school and college students and educators of any age, $50 for over-60s, $60 for everyone else, with couple and supporter tiers above that; it also brings discounts on the Center's other calls and workshops. Images exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years are not eligible. The Center takes no commission — the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. Submissions close 6 November 2026, selections are announced 15 November, and the exhibition runs 1 December 2026 to 31 January 2027. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $5 per image (membership from $25/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — Black, White & More
item.description: The SE Center's open call on monochrome — images produced with a single hue rather than recording the colours of the thing photographed. The Center is looking for all forms of monochrome imagery, black-and-white and toned photography alike, any subject, analog, digital or antique processes, and photographers of every skill level and location may enter. The juror is Jennifer Schlesinger, an artist, curator, gallerist and educator based in Santa Fe whose own practice runs through the historical development of photography as an artistic medium — from the camera obscura to the nineteenth-century albumen process to twentieth-century gelatin silver printing, which along with albumen are her chosen mediums; her work mostly concerns landscape and how humans interact philosophically with the natural world. Between thirty-five and forty selected images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $35 for up to five images and $6 for each additional image to a maximum of fifteen; members pay $28 and $5. Work exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years is not eligible, and there are no refunds for images not selected. The Center takes no commission — the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. Submissions opened 16 September 2026 and close 1 December; selections are announced 15 December and the exhibition opens 9 January 2027. One warning the organiser has not reconciled: the prospectus calendar reads “Submissions Close 12/1/26, Selections Announced 12/15/26, Exhibition Opens 1/9/27”, but the SE Center's own Smarter Entry board lists this call as closing 15 November — the same date it gives The Portrait. Enter by 15 November to be safe. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $35/5 images ($28 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portals · Collage Artists of America
item.description: Collage Artists of America, a Los Angeles society founded in 1988, opens its annual juried exhibition to members and non-members alike on the theme of portals. The organisers ask you to explore what defines a portal and to imagine one that resonates: an elaborate doorway leading to the known or the unknown, an opening into other universes or into the body or mind, any entrance to something real or imagined. Four kinds of work qualify — collage (flat or very low relief), mixed-media collage (moderate relief and/or different techniques and materials), assemblage (highly dimensional, multiple three-dimensional elements and/or freestanding) and digital collage, which the organisers define as a combination of multiple images and explicitly distinguish from digital manipulation of a single image, which does not qualify. For photographers that is the boundary to note: the prospectus never uses the word photograph in either direction, so the way in is the digital-collage definition itself - a photomontage is a combination of multiple images and qualifies, while a single unaltered frame does not. Nothing on any surface bars photographic material, and because the show is virtual there is no print or framing rule to fall foul of. The juror is Karin Skiba, who took her MFA at Claremont Graduate University, taught as a full-time art professor at Norco College and retired as Professor Emeritus, founded and directed the Norco College Art Gallery, was the inaugural director of the Hi-Desert Art Gallery and has curated at Joshua Tree's Juniper Arts Gallery. Awards total $1,300: $500 first place, $300 second, $200 third, a $100 Carolann Watterson Memorial Award and up to four honourable mentions of $50 each. Entry is $40 for one work and $5 for each of up to three additional works for non-members, or $35 for up to four works for members; membership costs $55 and the entry maximum is four works either way. Work shown at any prior juried CAA exhibit is ineligible, as is work made in an instructor-directed, step-by-step class or workshop, and artificially generated artwork is not accepted. The exhibition is virtual only, hosted on the CAA website and on OnlineJuriedShows, and runs 1 November to 31 December 2026 with an online reception and awards on 1 November. CAA takes no commission on sales. Entries close 1 October 2026 at 11:59 PT and the jury's decisions are announced on 12 October. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $40 for 1 image + $5 each additional ($35/4 members). Prize: $1,300 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Draw the Line · Museum of Northern California Art
item.description: The Museum of Northern California Art in Chico invites artists to submit work for Draw the Line, a juried exhibition showcasing drawings of all kinds. The museum leans deliberately into a broad definition: it is seeking work where mark-making, line and gesture are the primary language, made with traditional and non-traditional tools on conventional and unconventional surfaces, including digital line work and three-dimensional material 'drawn' in a way that blurs the boundary between drawing and sculpture. The accepted-media line is 'All media', with one exclusion: no giclée prints of original art or non-photographic art will be accepted — a bar on reproductions rather than on photographs, and nothing on any surface excludes photographic or lens-based work. Photographers should read the theme honestly, though: this is a drawing show, and the work has to speak the language of line. Eligibility is regional — original work by artists residing in Northern California, which the museum defines as a named list of 41 counties from Del Norte and Siskiyou down to San Mateo, Santa Clara, Merced and Mariposa. Selection is made by the museum's exhibition committee of professional artists and art collectors. Entry through the museum's own form is $35 for up to three works, $25 for monca members, and $10 for each additional piece; entering instead through CaFÉ, where the museum keeps a parallel listing, prices the first image at $15 with $10 for each additional image to a maximum of eight, so a single entry is cheaper by that route while three works cost $35 either way. Fees are non-refundable and there is no refund if the work is not accepted. AI work and work previously exhibited at monca will be disqualified. Accepted work must arrive ready to hang, fitted with framing wire because the museum hangs from a picture rail — sawtooth hangers are disqualified — and must stay up until the exhibition closes. Sales carry a 50 percent museum commission, and shipping, packaging and insurance are the artist's responsibility. Entries and payment close 4 October 2026 at 5pm, the jury notifies by email on or before 18 October, and the exhibition runs 19 November 2026 to 10 January 2027 with a reception on 20 November. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $35/3 images ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Flora & Fauna · South x Southeast Photo Gallery
item.description: South x Southeast's Flora & Fauna is curated by gallery director Nancy McCrary and framed by E. O. Wilson's line that we should preserve every scrap of biodiversity as priceless while we learn to use it and come to understand what it means to humanity — Wilson being the American biologist and naturalist often called Darwin's natural heir. The call sets no further brief than the title, and the gallery illustrates it with two of McCrary's own pictures: tick weed and water lilies in the Okefenokee Swamp in late winter, and early morning in the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya. Selected photographs hang in the SxSE Gallery through November and December 2026 — a virtual gallery whose own tagline is "making the virtual a reality" — and a Zoom group review is held with the exhibiting photographers during that run, on a date to be announced. Entry is by email to the gallery director: images should be JPEG only, 72dpi and 1000 pixels on the longest side, named lastname-firstname-title (the gallery's own example is mccrarynancybigredhouse), zipped into a single file and attached to an email with the subject line "Flora & Fauna". The entry fee is $40 for the first four images and $10 for each additional image, paid separately through the gallery's shop. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $40 for 4 images; $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Dear Fear: An Anthology
item.description: Dear Fear is an anthology of letters written to "fear foods" — the foods and drinks that trigger intense anxiety, guilt, panic or distress — by people in eating disorder recovery, with images by contributing visual artists set alongside poems, essays and other creative nonfiction. The editors chose the constrained form deliberately, merging the epistle with the apostrophe (an address to a non-living thing) to bring their writers' voices into the same room, where they can hear one another beyond the characteristics that culture says should divide them. The call welcomes emerging writers and artists and particularly encourages submissions from communities that have historically faced resistance to representation, including LGBT+, BIPOC and disabled communities; the editors also note the relative lack of literature by men about eating disorders and recovery, and hope to make space for those voices. Visual artists and makers of hybrid work may submit up to five images, as JPG/JPEG only, 1,200 pixels on the longest side, sRGB, named FirstName_LastName_1.jpg; prose and poetry are submitted through Duotrope and visual work through a Google form that requires signing in to a Google account. Be aware that the organisers enumerate no media at all — the category is simply "Visual Art and Hybrid Work", and the word photograph appears nowhere on the submission page, the anthology's own Duotrope listing or the rest of the site; nothing excludes photography either, and the file specification admits it. What signals the visual intent is the masthead: the visual editor is Roula Seikaly, described on the anthology's own site as an independent curator, writer and Co-Director at Humble Arts Foundation whose curatorial practice addresses contemporary photography and new media, and who has curated exhibitions at SF Camerawork, Blue Sky Gallery, Colorado Photographic Arts Center and Photographic Center Northwest. The poetry editor is Danielle Coffyn and the nonfiction editor is Maggie Russell. Hybrid works involving video, music or other streaming content are not accepted at this time, and material generated by artificial intelligence cannot be accepted. Previously published work is ineligible, though the editors do not count work posted on a platform you control — a personal blog, newsletter or social account — as published; simultaneous submissions are welcome with prompt notice if the work is taken elsewhere. The submission fee is $3 and is waived on request, and optional editorial feedback from the editors costs $30; all fees go towards paying contributors, and accepted work receives what the editors call a modest honorarium, which they do not quantify. They aim to respond within three months, and will make accommodations for submissions from justice-involved or unhoused writers and artists, and from people submitting on their behalf. The submission window runs 1 August to 15 October 2026, and the anthology is anticipated to publish in February 2027 with Sheila-Na-Gig, a nonprofit poetry journal and small press. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $3 (waived on request). Prize: Publication + cash honorarium.

item.title: Conservation · Black Eyes Gallery
item.description: Black Eyes Gallery's second call asks a single question — what would you save? Conservation wants photographs of the land, buildings, species and traditions the photographer most wants still to be there in the future: cottonwoods on the U.S.–Mexico border that have stood two hundred years, acres of the Amazon already gone, plants and animals lost daily and mostly never photographed, buildings pulled down faster than anyone can record them, people threatened with destruction. The gallery's framing is that a photograph outlasts what it points at, and that the record is the one form of keeping available to almost anyone. Any genre is welcome so long as the work is photographic or lens based, and anything created entirely or substantially with artificial intelligence is disqualified. Twenty-five images are selected by juror Douglas Fur, a nationally exhibited Tucson photographer with a 2006 BFA from Cornish College of the Arts who spent two years at Decode Gallery and is now Artist Liaison and Gallery Manager for Tucson Erotica. Selected photographers send a file and nothing else: the gallery prints, mats and frames every accepted image at its own expense for the show at 485 S. Stone from 3 to 28 November 2026, then holds the single exhibition print in its archive for two years before destroying it. Accepted work also enters a permanent online archive carrying the artist's name, image title and social link, and is promoted across the gallery's social channels, email list and website with an individual feature on the Black Eyes Instagram. Entry is $40 for up to five images or $50 for up to ten; a reduced $20 fee is held for two artists per call on a first-come, first-served basis for anyone who writes in before submitting, and any entry that produces no selection earns $5 off the next one. Submissions are reviewed blind where possible, on creativity, originality, interpretation of the theme and how an image works against the exhibition as a whole, with CV and bio largely set aside. Work may optionally be offered for sale at a price the artist sets, the gallery retaining 50 per cent, and photographers keep full copyright throughout. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $50/10. Prize: Exhibition.
